anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: This is the closest same-level anchor. Its L1 instance has four diamonds, visible material hazards, one screen and one support, with a depth-sorted canvas and a finite sequence of rotations and mining clicks. Museum L1 has more distinct input verbs and two timed waits, but each exhibit still asks for one final gesture, uses a large plinth, and exposes title clues; it has no changing voxel geometry, ray-occlusion decision, hazard management, or precision click target. Both are multi-action low-level tasks, so action count alone does not move Museum above L1.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: Cursor L2 is a single-goal active visual search: two decoys and 26 noise stars respond to a moving lens, and the final click must be within a 28 pixel radius of the hidden convergence point. Museum L1 has ten semantic actions and a small dependency chain, but the titles directly clue the gesture, the plinth is 120 by 92 pixels, and there is no comparable visual localization or decoy discrimination. The nearest easier anchor is unavailable because this assigned profile is already L1; Cursor L2 is the nearest harder comparison.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: Gyroscopic Tilt Board L3 is a continuously changing physical-control problem: three ordered lamps, three walls, three wells, momentum and friction, 50 ms ticks, and minimum physical evidence must all be satisfied before the cup. Museum L1 has no moving world and no repeated steering correction; hold and dwell wait on static predicates, while its other gestures are one-shot. The gyro's live control loop and collision recovery are materially above Museum's flat event recognition.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: Blind Dice Courier L4 requires planning a 48 to 105 roll route through an 18 by 11 warehouse, tracking a changing six-face orientation between sparse scanners, and crossing five face-gated barriers in order. Museum L1 has a static bounded room, one gesture per case, and visible title clues; none of its state is hidden across long movement or updated by physics. This is a substantially harder stateful spatial-memory task.

Every swap can trigger deterministic gravity/refill and multi-wave scoring; the final receipt must hit an exact target without touching black licorice. Museum L1 has no changing board, score route, terminal hazard, or multi-step board planning, so it is clearly below this high anchor.

visible_baseline_solution: A screenshot-only agent reads the wall ledger and the ten visible vocabulary labels. The titles are direct clues: Second Tap means double, Other Hand means right click, Long Journey means a drag across the plinth, Lingering Touch means a two-second static hold, Deepest Floor means scroll to the bottom, Growing Room means resize the room, The Withdrawal means leave and return, Perfect Stillness means a five-second dwell, Held Companion means Shift plus click, and Together Apart means the simultaneous a plus s chord. At composition 1 each case recipe contains only its final gesture, although gated cases after the first three remain veiled until their earlier case opens. The agent performs available gestures inside the visible room, waits for the hold or dwell task-clock predicate, and follows the newly revealed ledger until all ten cases are found. It then presses Close the exhibition. The normal UI path needs no private state: it uses the plinth, room scroll, resize handle, pointer enter/leave, keyboard modifiers, and visible ledger; the grader accepts only the event transcript produced by the selected input surface.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The active baseline is exactly difficulty 1/full. The generator uses composition 1, so each case has a one-gesture recipe; gated prerequisites still require a short visible unlock progression. This is a broad event-vocabulary task with timed static predicates, not a static one-click task, but its state does not change through a physical world, its titles clue the actions, and its plinth affords broad coordinates. It is comparable to the approved L1 Isometric Voxel Extraction Mine and remains below Cursor L2's active visual localization, Gyroscopic L3's continuous physics, Blind Dice L4's hidden orientation route, and Exact-Change L5's changing-board search. Full native input increases motor/interface burden as the separate interaction knob; it does not add composition or stateful planning, so it is not credited as a higher difficulty level.

findings.claim: The composition note says other recognized gestures interrupt the sequence, but a plain single tap is visibly recognized without changing recipe history.
findings.causal_explanation: The native up handler emits tap for an ordinary stationary click. Gallery.emit appends every emission to recognized but updates used/history only when the value is in the named gestures set; tap is not in that set. Therefore an agent can interleave plain taps without shifting the composition suffix. This is source-proven as a wording/behavior mismatch, but it is not a complete solve bypass because the required named prefix and final gesture still have to be emitted.

evidence.explanation: The valid gesture set excludes tap, while history updates are conditional on membership in that set.
A stationary unmodified click emits tap.
The visible composition note claims other recognized gestures interrupt the sequence.

findings.recommended_action: Confirm whether tap should be an intentional non-gesture. If it should interrupt, clear or advance history on tap; otherwise revise the composition note. Calibrate impact before changing any level label.

concise_summary: Keep the assigned difficulty-1/full baseline. Source shows a title-clued ten-gesture gallery with one-gesture recipes and a short gated unlock chain, below the approved L2-L5 stateful/search anchors. Composition 2 through 5 are distinguished by longer sampled prefixes and prerequisite cases in both input modes; fixed waits, geometry, and budget are not credited as profile increases. Full and simplified are source-equivalent semantic surfaces with mode-bound grading, pending runtime validation.

Historical pre-controls behavior is not established; current default versus explicit L1 equivalence is only a source comparison and challenge IDs intentionally differ.
The tap behavior finding depends on whether the visible phrase intended to include non-vocabulary taps.
